content: To apply eye drops, first wash your hands thoroughly. If you are wearing contact lenses, remove them before using the drops. Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly above your eye and instill one drop into the pouch. Look downward and gently close your eyes for 1 to 2 minutes. To prevent the medication from draining out, place one finger at the inner corner of your eye (near the nose) and apply gentle pressure for 2 to 3 minutes. Avoid blinking and do not rub your eye. Do not rinse the dropper. Replace the dropper cap after each use. If you are using another type of eye medication, such as drops or ointments, wait at least 5 to 10 minutes before applying the other medication. If this medication is prescribed for regular use, ensure you use it consistently to achieve the maximum benefit. To help you remember, use it at the same times each day. Common side effects may include burning, stinging, redness of the eye, eye irritation, or temporary blurred vision. These effects are usually mild and temporary. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Before using homatropine hydrobromide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to belladonna alkaloids (such as atropine), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. After applying this medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred, and your eyes may become more sensitive to light. Protect your eyes in bright light conditions. Infants and small children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug. Ensure that this medication does not enter a child’s mouth. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you miss a dose of this medication and are on a regular schedule, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for proper disposal instructions. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
